pr_body:
# Support injecting keyed services with `[Inject]`

This PR adds support for injecting keyed services into Blazor components using the `[Inject]` attribute.

## Description

API diff:

```diff
namespace Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components;

[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Property, AllowMultiple = false, Inherited = true)]
public sealed class InjectAttribute : Attribute
{
+    /// <summary>
+    /// Gets or sets the object that specifies the key of the service to inject.
+    /// </summary>
+    public object? Key { get; init; }
}
```

Fixes #50374

issue_context.body: This was added to .NET in preview7, we should support this within `[Inject]` attribute and update the `@inject` directive to support providing a key as a constant string.

review_comments:
This is interesting! Pranav did a cull of all our uses of `Select(lambda)` but looks like this - which I see you're bringing forwards from the old code - escaped, perhaps because it's in `Shared`.

Totally fine to leave as-is but if you decide to make other changes here might be nice to swap this over to building the array manually.
We can file an issue to track removing it.
Any reason `[FromKeyedServices(...)]` can't be used instead of `[Inject]`?
It should be a totally possible alternative - it just isn't consistent with the existing Blazor experience. I'm definitely open to considering it as an alternative, though.

@MackinnonBuck @BrennanConroy `[FromKeyedServices]` is not suitable in this context.

`Inject` is the Blazor/Razor specific attribute that the Razor compiler targets for the `@inject` directive, which is what our activator looks for, and it doesn't have a dependency on ASP.NET Core.

Looking at the caller, it seems you could pass in `IServiceProvider` and do the `IServiceProvider is IServiceProviderIsKeyedService keyedServiceProvider && keyedServiceProvider.IsKeyedService(...)` check and throw early if keyed services aren't supported.

Good point. The thing is, though, that `ComponentFactory` in its current state isn't limited to using a single `IServiceProvider` instance, so it might not always be correct to verify the existence of a service on the first `IServiceProvider` and reuse that result for future `IServiceProvider`s.

Also, it might happen that we create/cache a property injector but never invoke it, in which case we throw an exception unnecessarily. For example, it's possible that a component could have an interactive render mode that disables prerendering, so the component never actually gets rendered by the endpoint renderer (and we hit that final `else` block in `InstantiateComponent()`). In this case, the component might require a service unavailable during prerendering but available during interactive rendering, and we would throw an exception unnecessarily.

So, I'm thinking it might be best to leave the validation at the point when `[Inject]` properties are populated. Does that seem reasonable?

We can constraint this further to a string I think, as I believe the scenarios where you take a non-string value are for things like fallback registrations via `KeyedService.AnyKey`. In the context of the compiler this is going end up something like `@inject "key" ServiceType Property`.

Are nonstring keys meant to be supported in non-Blazor cases in general? If so it might be nice to leave the option of using them with `[Inject]` even if you can't use them with `@inject`.

Of course, you'd be limited to compile-time constant values since this is an attribute, so I'm not totally clear on what useful use cases there are for this.
Yes, that was the reasoning with just going for string directly
Well, this might be ok as object. You could also use an Enum here and we would be precluding that, so I retract my comment here.
